speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you have a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities, along with recent fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. To help me determine the cause, can you tell me when these symptoms started and if anyone around you is currently sick?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Scarlet Fever (Group A Streptococcus) or Erythema Infectiosum (Parvovirus B19). Given the specific description of a facial rash sparing the perioral area appearing 4 days after initial respiratory symptoms, Parvovirus B19 (Fifth Disease) is the most likely diagnosis, though Scarlet Fever remains a strong differential. I will request a complete blood count and C-reactive protein to look for leukocytosis and elevated inflammatory markers. REQUEST TEST: CBC, CRP
